In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermal effects of RF and gradient coils are both relevant, and should be considered when assessing the safety of metallic implants in MRI.

, in the MR community, the attention should be paid not only to RF fields, but also to GFs, when considering metallic implants, because the latter are able to produce a significant heating, which may affect the tissues indirectly, and this effect may become important when dealing with large implants.

the current density J can become significant for a metallic implant exposed to GF, even if the magnetic field B is small.
